| [CLAIM-157](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md) v7 | Relative to a stated target, a combined form is one system while its joint dynamics are nearly decomposable with the form as a block whose gap beats the Occam factor, and it lasts as long as that block persists; the unit is the gap-isolated block, not any member | The record's proposed answer to [QUESTION-035](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md), joining the dual-filed MOM results. Simon's near-decomposability says what to compare: interaction inside a candidate block against interaction across its edge. The gap theorem says the unit is the block, and the Occam factor says when the gap is big enough to name it. Persistence is how long the block keeps clearing the threshold. It answers the owner's "privileged nomenclature" for the dancing couple with a test. Proposed: nothing has been measured. | [CLAIM-165](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-165.md) v2 | A combined form constituted by mutual entrainment is not thereby a self in the subject sense: two dancers in phase are one coordination, an autonomous process, and still two subjects | The record's own objection to [CLAIM-172](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-172.md), narrowed in version 2 after the owner's reply ([CLAIM-175](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-175.md)). | [CLAIM-172](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-172.md) v8 | Mutual entrainment is a sufficient mark of a combined form, and marks it as one of peers: when each side adjusts the other's timing the pair carries a collective variable neither has alone; one-way drive also makes a combined form, with a hierarchical architecture | The record's reading in answer to the owner's prompt of 2026-10-11, "connect extended self to entrainment". Clark & Chalmers' marks of extension are availability marks, and the coupling-constitution objection says coupling does not entail parthood. Mutual entrainment sidesteps the objection rather than answering it: it individuates a new system by its collective variable. It does not cover a passive store like Otto's notebook, which is coupled across time by writing and reading, not by timing. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-173](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-173.md) v3 | The threshold criterion measures coupling strength, and coupling is not constitution: a metronome driving a musician, or a nerve driving a muscle, forms a strongly coupled block that clears the threshold without being one system | The record's anticipated objection to [CLAIM-157](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md), and Adams & Aizawa's coupling-constitution objection ([LIT-455](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-455.md)) aimed at the new criterion. Near-decomposability is about the size of couplings, not their direction. One-way drive can make a tightly coupled block. The entrainment claim excluded exactly this case. Rejected on the owner's challenge (CLAIM-167): they should pass, and direction gives a system's architecture, not its membership. | Rejected |
